title: The Date of the "Cyclopean Wall" at Hebron
author: David Ussishkin
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted peer-reviewed journal article. Project stores its own summary of the argument only; no reproduction of the article's text, plans, or photographs.
summary: Ussishkin challenges the standard dating (Eisenberg's Middle Bronze II attribution, based on pottery/scarabs from floors associated with the wall) of Tell Rumeida's massive 'cyclopean' city wall and its abutting glacis, arguing instead that both were built during the later Iron Age, when Hebron was a fortified city of the kingdom of Judah, rather than in the Middle Bronze Age with a later Iron Age reuse. If correct, this would remove the cyclopean wall as evidence for any Iron I/early Iron IIA (10th century BCE) fortification phase at the site altogether, pushing its actual construction later than even the Iron II horizon Eisenberg and Ben-Shlomo (2017) already attribute to nearby glacis/rampart elements. This project cites Ussishkin to disclose that even the wall most often invoked for an early Iron Age Hebron fortification is itself under live scholarly dispute — not to adopt his redating as settled.
